headline: High: oh-my-openagent’s broad network/browser/MCP surface can leak or misapply content when paired with a content-writing agent, while shared-file and prompt-injection paths remain plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no runtime isolation or I/O surfaces documented, so direct injection is not proven. Profile B explicitly uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, browsers, and shared files, which can ingest external content and pass it into agent workflows. The pair therefore has a plausible instruction-hijack path via B, but A alone does not create it.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests content from browsers, MCPs, or shared files without provenance checks
IF agent_a-generated text is forwarded into agent_b tool prompts or hooks
mitigations: Disable browser-to-agent auto-ingest in agent_b
Add provenance tags to all MCP/file inputs in agent_b
Route agent_a output through a human review step before agent_b consumes it
requires-engineering: sandbox shared-file inputs for agent_b

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches session history, project code, AGENTS.md/README.md, and provider auth data, and has broad network egress. Agent A is a docs-only content-writing repo with no data classes touched, so the main leakage risk is B exporting shared workspace or secrets-derived context; A does not add a separate sensitive sink. The shared-workspace path is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent_b is pointed at a workspace containing secrets or private code
IF agent_b sends session history or file contents to external APIs during normal operation
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace before launch
Restrict agent_b network egress to approved domains
Separate agent_b from sensitive repos and auth files
Rotate provider auth data if it was exposed to agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or network capabilities documented, but agent B can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and use multiple writable files and MCP-backed actions. Because A is non-runnable and B is task-scoped, direct write-write conflict is not established; however, uncertainty remains about shared mutable resources, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same workspace or config directory
IF agent_b subprocesses modify files that agent_a later reads or summarizes
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared files
Run agent_b with least-privilege filesystem access
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing source, and agent B has action-capable surfaces such as team_send_message, team_task_create, and browser/network access. If B treats A’s generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions or messages. A does not verify facts, and B’s toolset makes downstream impact more than a simple formatting issue.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a output into team_send_message or task creation without verification
IF agent_a produces unsupported claims that agent_b uses as facts
mitigations: Require citation checks before agent_b acts on agent_a output
Insert a verification step between agents
Limit agent_b to drafting, not sending, until reviewed
requires-engineering: add structured confidence metadata to agent_a outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles provider auth prompts, installation identifiers, session history, and project code, while A is a docs-only repository with no data classes. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk if B processes regulated or sensitive workspace data under its broader telemetry and network behavior. A is not the compliance driver here, so only B is cited.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in agent_b’s session history or project code context
IF retention or telemetry settings are not disabled for agent_b
mitigations: Review telemetry and retention settings in agent_b
Avoid placing regulated data in agent_b workspaces
Separate auth prompts from sensitive projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
